newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells U.S. to speak with one voice on Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China tells U.S. to speak with one voice on Taiwan.

text.p: China on Thursday told the United States to speak with one voice on Beijing's arch-rival Taiwan after U.S. House Speaker Newt Gingrich vowed Washington would support the island against mainland attack.

The United States would appear ridiculous if sections of its government followed separate foreign policies, and Washington should live up to its promises not to interfere in Taiwan, said Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang.
Gingrich, speaker of the House of Representatives, ended an Asian tour in Taiwan on Wednesday, hailing democracy on the island as a model for its communist rival on the mainland.
Gingrich also stood by his controversial pledge that U.S. forces would defend Taiwan against Chinese attack.
"There are contradictions in the words of U.S. leaders, including leaders of Congress," Chinese spokesman Shen told a news briefing in Beijing.

Washington had promised many times it would not support independence for Taiwan, which Beijing considers a rebel province, and had vowed not to interfere with Taipei's peaceful reunification with the mainland, Shen said.
"We have seen that the words of the U.S. government including some leaders of other departments are different from their promises," he said when asked about Gingrich's remarks.

As a big power and permanent member of the United Nations Security Council, the United States should match its actions with its promises, he said, adding that Washington should speak with one diplomatic voice.
"We even more do not wish to see all the departments of the U.S. government carrying out different foreign policies," he said. "That would be very laughable."

China says it wants peaceful reunification with Taiwan, separated since defeated Nationalist armies fled to the island at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, but has vowed to invade if Taipei declares independence.

President Bill Clinton sent warships near Taiwan one year ago in a show of force as Beijing held war games and missile tests in a bid to intimidate the island as it held its first direct presidential election.

Officials of the Democratic administration have sought to play down the Republican congressman's tough talk of defending Taiwan, saying only that any attack on the island by China would be a matter of grave concern.

Gingrich criticised Beijing over its human rights record during the Chinese leg of his whirlwind Asian tour, but was full of praise for Taiwan's democratic reforms during a three-hour visit to the island on Wednesday.
"Taiwan has completed a remarkable journey to full democracy," the speaker said.

"Taiwan's elected legislature and the recent inauguration of the first popularly elected president in over 4,000 years of Chinese history, provide a model not only for the People's Republic of China, but for the world," he said.
